title: Patterns: Repeating Patterns and Number Patterns
seo_title: Grade 1 Patterns Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Copy and extend simple patterns using physical objects and drawings; create own patterns; describe patterns; number patterns: sequences in ones, twos, fives and tens.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 1 maths worksheets: repeating patterns, what comes next, and number patterns in 2s, 5s and 10s. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Find the part that repeats: red, blue, red, blue…
  • Say the pattern out loud to hear what comes next.
  • Number patterns can count in 2s, 5s or 10s.
  • Check by continuing the pattern again.

Examples

Example

2, 4, 6, 8, …

add 2 each time

Answer: 10

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong placeContinue from the last item.
Not repeatingThe unit must repeat exactly.
SkippingKeep the same step.

faq.a: Grade R to Grade 3 in South African schools. Learners are about 6 to 7 years old in Grade 1.
Repeating patterns of objects and shapes, and number patterns.

faq.q: What is the core of a pattern?

faq.a: Yes, counting back is a pattern too.

items.q: What goes in the two gaps? Read from left to right.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: The numbers repeat. The repeating unit is 1, 2. The last unit is finished, so start again. Next is 1. 3 is counting on, not repeating.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: The numbers repeat. The repeating unit is 1, 2, 3. The last unit is finished, so start again. Next is 1. 4 is counting on, not repeating.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: The numbers repeat. The repeating unit is 5, 5, 8. The last unit so far is 5, 5. Next is 8. 6 is counting on, not repeating.

items.e: The numbers repeat. The repeating unit is 2, 7, 7. The last unit is finished, so start again. Next is 2. 8 is counting on, not repeating.

items.q: How many socks? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 socks. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. There are 6 socks.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 8 + 2 = 10. 9 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many eyes? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each child has 2 eyes. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. There are 8 eyes.

items.q: How many shoes? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 shoes. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. There are 8 shoes.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 16 + 2 = 18. 17 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many socks? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 socks. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. There are 10 socks.

items.q: Count in 2s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. When you count in 2s from 0, every number is even. 7, 9 and 15 are odd.

items.q: Each stick has 10 cubes. How many cubes?
items.e: Each stick has 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. There are 30 cubes.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 30 + 10 = 40. 31 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 10s.
items.e: Each child shows 2 hands. That is 10 fingers. Count in 10s: 10, 20. There are 20 fingers.

items.q: Each ten frame is full. How many counters?
items.e: A full ten frame has 10 counters. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. There are 50 counters.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 60 + 10 = 70. 61 is counting in 1s.

items.q: Each stick has 10 cubes. How many cubes?
items.e: Each stick has 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. There are 60 cubes.

items.q: Which one counts in 10s?
items.e: Counting in 10s, each number is 10 more: 20, 30, 40. 20, 21, 22 is 1s, 20, 22, 24 is 2s and 20, 25, 30 is 5s.

items.q: Ayanda made a repeating pattern, but she made one mistake. Which bead is wrong?
items.e: The repeating unit is yellow, yellow, blue. Say it along the row. Bead 7 should be yellow, so 7 is wrong.

items.q: Lindiwe made a repeating pattern, but she made one mistake. Which shape is wrong?
items.e: The repeating unit is circle, star, triangle. Say it along the row. Shape 8 should be star, so 8 is wrong.

items.q: Kabelo threads this repeating unit 3 times. How many beads does he use?
items.e: Each unit has 3 beads. 3, 6, 9. Kabelo uses 9 beads. 6 is only 2 beads in each unit.

items.q: Ofentse makes this repeating unit 5 times. How many flags are there?
items.e: Each unit has 2 flags. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. There are 10 flags. 5 counts the units, not the flags.

items.q: Bongani draws this repeating unit 2 times. How many shapes does he draw?
items.e: Each unit has 4 shapes. 4 + 4 = 8. 4 is only one unit. 2 counts the units.

items.q: Tumi keeps going with this pattern. She uses 8 red beads in all. How many blue beads does she use?
items.e: The unit is red, blue. Each red bead has one blue bead after it. 8 red beads, so 8 blue beads.

items.q: Karabo threads beads. What colour is the next bead?

items.q: Lethabo hangs flags for the swimming gala. What colour is the next flag?

items.q: Fatima claps and stamps in a pattern. What does she do next?

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next?

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.

items.q: How many petals? Count in 5s.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next?

items.q: Count in 5s from 0. How do the numbers end?
items.e: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 … The last digit goes 0, 5, 0, 5. So they always end in 0 or 5.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 20 fingers.

items.q: Count in 5s. What number is missing?
How many petals? Count in 5s.

items.q: Count back in 5s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 less. 40 − 5 = 35. 39 is counting back in 1s.
